ruling.recommended_action: Record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file (no monetary refund is due on this fixed-quote RydeX trip) and send the driver's account to Ryde review for repeated route deviations.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeX (non-metered) trip: the fare is a fixed booking quotation, so mileage driven does not change the fare [F6][RD-2]. The GPS record nonetheless shows an off-route segment: 14:19–14:26, 5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, +3.64 km and up to 1160 m off the optimal route [F3], against the shortest-and-most-direct duty in [RD-1]. The whole trip ran 15.2 km / 23.2 min versus an optimal 10.7 km / 17.3 min [F1][F2], and the billed distance of 10.68 km did not exceed the 10.7 km optimal [F4][F6] — so the rider paid nothing for the extra distance.

The only explanation on record is the driver's post-trip statement "The GPS rerouted me, that's all" [F8]. There is no in-app chat at all [F7], so no rider message before 14:19 sent any agreement covering this segment; a driver's untimestamped post-trip statement is a claim, not consent [F8][RD-5]. The segment therefore counts as an unexcused deviation (both advocates stipulate this ground), and my segment finding below rests on that reading: consent_after_or_none → counts [F3][F7][RD-1][RD-5].

RD-4 cannot rescue the segment: the only traffic records are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the AYE and CTE [F9][F10], which is neither band 1 nor band 2, and there is no traffic incident near the route in the trip window [F11][RD-4(a)][RD-4(b)]. Weather was fair [F12], so no other reasonable cause is evidenced.

On money, [RD-2]'s non-metered branch refunds only ERP/tolls actually incurred on an unexcused segment and any unpublished post-trip add-on. The bill is base $3.90 + distance $15.06 + time $4.50 + platform $1.47, with $0.00 waiting, no surge and no toll or ad-hoc item [F5][F6]. The refundable amount is therefore $0.00, and [RD-2] directs no_action while recording the RD-1 breach; [FARE-1] adds nothing, as no unpublished item was charged, and [FARE-2] is not triggered (no toll field).

[RD-6] is a separate ladder: because an RD-1 breach is recorded in this case and the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2, with 4 disputes in 90 days and 2 upheld on route [F14], this is a repeated breach and an account flag attaches. The flag is driven only by the profile field as the additional action RD-6 requires; the profile was not used to decide whether the deviation occurred — that rested on [F3][F7][F8][F1]. The rider's profile [F13] (0 upheld) is relevant to nothing and I do not rely on it.

segment_findings.reason: The only message-like record is the driver's post-trip statement "The GPS rerouted me, that's all" [F8], written after the trip and not part of the chat, and the chat record contains no messages at all [F7]. No rider message sent before the segment's 14:19 start agrees to this route, and a driver's claim of agreement in his own statement is not consent [RD-5]. Nothing in [F3] is a rider-named stop and no message reacts to the deviation, so the 5.03 km / +3.64 km segment is unexcused and counts under [RD-1] and [RD-2]; the driver's bare claim is answered by the recorded 1160 m divergence and the +4.5 km total [F1][F3].

rejected_claims.reason: Correct on the absence of consent (no chat at all [F7] and the post-trip statement [F8] is not consent), and I adopt the rider side's reading; but it does not support a monetary outcome: on this fixed-quote RydeX trip the billed distance did not exceed the optimal route [F4][F6], so [RD-2]'s non-metered branch yields $0 and the refundable amount is nil.

Accepted as a finding (the segment is unexempted, [F3][RD-1]), but it produces no refund: [RD-2] only refunds ERP/tolls and unpublished add-ons on non-metered services, and the bill contains none [F5][F6]. The outcome the claim implies, refund_partial, does not follow.

Granted in substance — the prior upheld route dispute [F14] satisfies RD-6 and I apply flag_account — but C6 asks for it alongside a refund under C2; the money figure is $0.00 [F4][F6][RD-2], so the flag rides on a no_action outcome with the RD-1 breach recorded, not on a refund.

Accepted that no detour mileage was billed [F4][F6], but it does not answer the case: [RD-1] is a duty to take the shortest and most direct route regardless of billing, and [F3] shows a 3.64 km unexcused deviation. Its implication that nothing is on the driver's record is wrong.

Accepted on the arithmetic — the bill holds no toll, waiting fee or post-trip add-on, so [RD-2]/[FARE-1] return $0.00 [F5][F6] — but RD-2 does not make the deviation disappear; it only fixes the monetary figure at nil while recording the breach.

Rejected: RD-6's predicate is met on the driver's own profile (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2, both route disputes [F14]) together with the RD-1 breach recorded in this case, so the account flag is warranted; the volume of trips and the rider's record [F13] are irrelevant to the driver's repetition.

Accepted as to the facts (no chat messages [F7]; the driver's statement is not consent [F8]) but the inference runs the other way: with no rider message of any kind, nothing consents to the 14:19–14:26 routing, so under [RD-5] the segment counts rather than being excused.

Accepted that the monetary figure is nil [F4][F6][RD-2] and I rule no_action; the claim that "nothing remains" is rejected — the RD-1 breach is recorded on the file and, given the prior upheld route dispute [F14], RD-6 account review attaches.
